entry.title: Among all species Humans are one of the best at long-distance endurance running.
entry.content:
A noteworthy ability of the Human species is to run for long, uninterrupted periods of time. Few species are better, and Humans are the only ape that is capable of it.

Among many others, specific traits which enable this include:

  • Taller body with more surface area which facilitates evaporative cooling (sweating)
  • Wider heel bone to better absorb impact
  • Longer legs enabling a greater stride

It is an ability that likely evolved in conjunction with Persistence Hunting, a technique which involves chasing an animal over long distances. The Human hunter can withstand the chase better than their prey, and eventually they will catch it even if initially the animal can run faster. If the hunter can keep chase long enough, the prey animal will either succumb to exhaustion, overheating or injury.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endurance_running_hypothesis

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persistence_hunting

Source: https://www.ucdavis.edu/blog/humans-are-born-run

entry.title: The Pygmalion Effect is a psychological phenomemon in which placing high expectations on someone leads to their better performance.
entry.content:
The Effect is an example of a self-fulfilling prophecy, the subject of the expectation performs better because of their belief that their performance is required, and not merely an optional choice.

The Pygmalion Effect is named for the sculptor Pygmalion from greek mythology. In his story he crafts a statue, and falls so intensely in love with his creation that it transforms into a real woman.

The term was coined by psychologists Robert Rosenthal and Lenore Jacombson. They conducted a study on school children in which the teacher expressed both high and low expectations on the students. As measured by IQ test scores, children who were expected to perform well had higher scores. Conversely, children who were expected to perform poorly by their teachers had lower scores.

Source: https://example.org

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pygmalion_effect

entry.title: People can be Ambiverted, meaning they are equal parts Introverted and Extroverted.
entry.content:
Introverted people obtain gratification from being alone, and consider social engagement to be mentally draining.

Extroverted people are the inverse of introverted, they are gratified and energized by being around others.

Ambiversion is a third personality trait at the mid point along a spectrum between introversion and extroversion. It was first proposed in 1923 by the American psychologist Edmund Smith Conklin.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extraversion_and_introversion#Ambiversion
